html:
Islam is the religion founded on the teaching of the Prophet Muhammad in Arabia in the early 600s, today the faith of about two billion people, a quarter of humanity. Its name means submission to God, and its followers are Muslims.

Muslims believe that from 610 in Mecca Muhammad received revelations from the one God, collected as the Quran. Islam sees him as the last of a line of prophets that includes Abraham, Moses and Jesus. Its practice rests on five pillars: the declaration of faith, five daily prayers, alms, the fast of Ramadan and the pilgrimage to Mecca. Muhammad's move to Medina in 622, the hijra, starts the Muslim calendar.

After his death in 632 the caliphs spread Arab rule from Spain to Central Asia within a century. A quarrel over who should lead, made bitter by the killing of Ali in 661 and of his son Husayn in 680, split the faith into Sunni and Shia branches.

Islam also spread without conquest, along trade routes: across the Sahara to West Africa, down the East African coast, and over the Indian Ocean to the Maldives and Sumatra, where Samudera Pasai was the first Muslim sultanate in the islands. Indonesia is now the largest Muslim country. Movements as different as Sufi orders and the American Nation of Islam draw on its language.
sum: Islam is the religion founded on the teaching of the Prophet Muhammad in Arabia in the early 600s, today the faith of about two billion people, a quarter of humanity. Its name means submission to God, and its followers are Muslims.
